title: Newton's Shell Theorem and Atom Instability Inside Black Holes
content: We apply Newton's Shell Theorem to the interior of a black hole modelled as a uniform-density sphere of mass and Schwarzschild radius. By the Shell Theorem, only the mass inside the radius contributes to gravity, maximal at the surface and zero at the centre. Gravitational pressure therefore has an ever-diminishing gradient towards the centre of a black hole. Comparing with standard Mott pressure-ionization thresholds, we show that Fe breaks essentially at the surface of a black hole,  68 m below the surface of Sgr A*, and never in the Earth. The region of instability is a skin, not a centre. There is no singularity to be crushed to, no firewall, and no information loss. Jets and winds are a release of energy from the skin where matter breaks.
